observed_original_abi.calling_convention_rationale: Four independent reads of the 25-instruction listing at 0x0068f9b0. (1) 0x0068f9b6 MOV EBX,ECX copies ECX -- an incoming register -- into the body-local callee-saved EBX, and no other instruction of the function reads ECX before it is overwritten at 0x0068f9c8 MOV ECX,ESI / 0x0068f9d8 MOV ECX,EDI; the receiver therefore arrives in ECX. (2) 0x0068f9df C2 04 00 is RET 0x4: the callee pops 4 bytes, so the caller does not clean and this is not cdecl. (3) __fastcall is excluded because EDX is dead on entry -- its first write in the body is the slot-0 dispatch load at 0x0068f9c6 MOV EDX,[EAX], and no instruction reads it before that -- so EDX is a scratch register here, not a second argument. (4) __stdcall is excluded because it carries no incoming register parameter at all, which (1) contradicts. A non-receiver callee-cleaned register-plus-one-word form does not exist, so __thiscall is the only convention consistent with all four.
observed_original_abi.receiver_adjustor_delta_evidence: No instruction of 0x0068f9b0 modifies ECX before its first read at 0x0068f9b6; there is no ADD/SUB on ECX anywhere in the 25 instructions, so the receiver is used at its entry value and the adjustor delta is zero.
observed_original_abi.return_type_rationale: No exit path writes EAX. The three JE targets are 0x0068f9dc (0x0068f9be, identity; 0x0068f9d1, null old pointer), and on the fall-through path the last write to EAX is 0x0068f9d3 MOV EAX,[EDI], an object pointer consumed immediately by 0x0068f9d5 MOV EDX,[EAX+0x4] and never by the epilogue. The early-out at 0x0068f9be leaves EAX as it was on entry. Nothing is defined on return, so the function is a procedure.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: Nothing is propagated. No path writes EAX with a result: the only EAX writes are the two object-pointer loads at 0x0068f9c4 and 0x0068f9d3, both consumed by the immediately following slot loads at 0x0068f9c6 and 0x0068f9d5. The identity exit at 0x0068f9be returns with EAX never written by this body at all. EAX is undefined on return on every path.
observed_original_abi.termination: RET 0x4 at 0x0068f9df (bytes C2 04 00, the last three bytes of the body)
observed_original_abi.stack_cleanup_evidence: The immediate operand of the RET at 0x0068f9df is 0x4, so the callee discards exactly one 4-byte word. The frame is balanced beforehand: PUSH EBX at 0x0068f9b0, PUSH ESI at 0x0068f9b1 and PUSH EDI at 0x0068f9b8 against POP EDI at 0x0068f9dc, POP ESI at 0x0068f9dd and POP EBX at 0x0068f9de, so the only net ESP change across the call is the 4 bytes RET 0x4 removes. The single ordinary stack slot is therefore one pointer wide.
observed_original_abi.saved_registers_evidence: PUSH EBX 0x0068f9b0, PUSH ESI 0x0068f9b1, PUSH EDI 0x0068f9b8, POP EDI 0x0068f9dc, POP ESI 0x0068f9dd, POP EBX 0x0068f9de -- three callee-saved registers, in matching order, each restored on every path because all three exits land on 0x0068f9dc.
observed_original_abi.stack_frame: none; no EBP is established and no frame pointer appears in the listing
observed_original_abi.ordinary_stack_argument_slots_note: One 4-byte ordinary stack argument, at entry_ESP+0x4, reclaimed by the callee through RET 0x4.

ordinary_stack_arguments.evidence: 0x0068f9b2 8B 74 24 0C MOV ESI,DWORD PTR [ESP+0x0C]. ESP arithmetic: on entry [ESP+0x0] holds the return address, so entry_ESP+0x4 is the first stack argument slot; PUSH EBX at 0x0068f9b0 moves ESP to entry_ESP-0x4 and PUSH ESI at 0x0068f9b1 moves it to entry_ESP-0x8, making [ESP+0x0C] == entry_ESP+0x4. The displacement is 0x0C and not 0x10 precisely because the load sits between the second and third pushes (PUSH EDI at 0x0068f9b8 comes after it).
ordinary_stack_arguments.read_once: Loaded exactly once at 0x0068f9b2 into ESI and never re-read from the stack; the captured value is reused by 0x0068f9bc (compare), 0x0068f9c0 (null test), 0x0068f9c8 (dispatch receiver), 0x0068f9cc (stored value). The function never writes to its own argument slot.
ordinary_stack_arguments.type: opaque 4-byte pointer; no pointee type is established by the bytes

indirect_dispatches.entered_on: the outgoing pointer, captured at 0x0068f9b9 before either dispatch (EDI)

indirect_dispatch_notes: Both dispatches read a dword from the object's own first word (the vptr at offset 0) and then a raw dword of that table, with no adjustment of the receiver between load and call: slot 0 at [EAX] and slot 1 at [EAX+0x4].

The semantic role of slot 0 and of slot 1 is NOT established by the bytes. A retain/acquire reading of slot 0 and a release/destroy reading of slot 1 is a plausible hypothesis and is unproven; nothing in this listing, in this function's own callees, or in the committed xref export identifies either entry. The slots are labelled by index only and no name is attached to them.

The roles are additionally unconstrained by the surrounding guard structure: the identity test, the null tests and the store-between-the-calls ordering are equally consistent with acquire/release, with a two-phase commit pair, or with unrelated bookkeeping. The evidence fixes the order and the guards, not the meaning.

No direct callee exists. The only transfers out of the body are the two indirect CALL EDX instructions at 0x0068f9ca and 0x0068f9da; the committed edge export knowledgegraph/triage/xrefs-2540f2ca.tsv records 50 inbound direct-call rows and no outbound edge for this VA, so the targets of the two dispatches are unconstrained by the export as well.

ordering.load_once: 0x0068f9b9 loads [EBX+0x8] into EDI before either dispatch. A body that re-read the field at 0x0068f9d3 would enter slot 1 on whatever slot 0 left behind; the captured EDI is what the listing uses.
ordering.store_between_calls: 0x0068f9cc MOV [EBX+0x8],ESI executes BETWEEN the two dispatches (after 0x0068f9ca, before 0x0068f9d5). Consequently slot 0 observes the OLD field value and slot 1 observes the NEW one. This ordering is load-bearing and is pinned by model-test case 3, whose slot hooks record the field value they observe.
ordering.null_argument_clears_field: 0x0068f9c0 TEST ESI,ESI / 0x0068f9c2 JE 0x0068f9cc -- the JE targets the STORE at 0x0068f9cc, not a point past it. A null argument therefore still clears the field, and only the equality test at 0x0068f9be skips the store.
ordering.identity_is_noop: 0x0068f9bc CMP ESI,EDI / 0x0068f9be JE 0x0068f9dc. The comparison is on the pointers themselves, so re-assigning the already-stored pointer runs neither slot and does not rewrite the field. Both-null takes the same exit.
ordering.old_pointer_null_guard: 0x0068f9cf TEST EDI,EDI / 0x0068f9d1 JE 0x0068f9dc -- guarded on the value captured at 0x0068f9b9, not on the field as it now stands.
ordering.all_exits_converge: 0x0068f9dc is the target of the JE at 0x0068f9be and of the JE at 0x0068f9d1, and the fall-through of the last CALL; every path reaches the same three pops and the same RET 0x4.

unresolved_questions: What are the concrete types of the receiver and of the dispatched object? The bytes name neither, and SporeApp.exe carries no RTTI.

What is the meaning of the dword at receiver+0x8, and what do the two slots called around the store actually do? A retain/acquire plus release reading is a hypothesis; the bytes fix only the order and the guards.
What are the concrete targets behind vtable slots 0 and 1? The xref export constrains neither, because both dispatches are indirect and no data reference to this VA exists.
Do the 50 direct callers all pass the same kind of object, or do the tables at 0x014018b0 / 0x0143dcc4 / 0x0143ddf4 correspond to several distinct receiver types?
Are the three recorded table occurrences genuine vtables at all? They mix code pointers with non-code words and no vtable pass has been run on this program.
What is the receiver's total size? Only the single dword at +0x8 is touched, so the surrounding layout is unknown.
runtime_gates: A live receiver whose +0x8 field differs from the incoming pointer is required for any dispatch to be observed; when they are equal (0x0068f9be) the body is a total no-op.

Both dispatched objects must carry a table with at least two dword slots before slot 0 can be entered; the machine test dereferences [obj] and then [table+0] and [table+0x4] unconditionally on the non-null path.

The two slot targets must be real thiscall functions taking only an ECX pointer; a differential run needs the concrete receiver type and the concrete slot implementations identified first, which the bytes do not establish.
notes: Authored from the 25-instruction body at 0x0068f9b0..0x0068f9e1, re-read in this session with objdump and cross-checked against the Ghidra function record. The reconstruction is total for this body: every instruction, displacement, branch, register and return is accounted for. Three properties a plausible rewrite loses are stated explicitly in observed_original_abi.ordering -- the field is loaded once and held, the store runs between the two dispatches, and the null-argument JE targets the store so a null argument clears the field. The identity of the function (name and normalized_symbol) is the index record's, sourced from the SDK decompilation export, and is recorded as corroboration only: no class, member, field or slot name is claimed from it. Both indirect dispatches are labelled by slot index alone, and the retain/release reading is explicitly marked unproven in indirect_dispatch_notes. The empty globals list is a corroborated absence: the datarefs sidecar has no row for this VA and the listing has no absolute-address memory operand.
